title: St. Innocent of Irkutsk in Mouravieff
subtitle: The first bishop of Irkutsk
source: A. N. Mouravieff, A History of the Church of Russia, ch. XVI, pp. 280-281, tr. R. W. Blackmore (A. N. Mouravieff, A History of the Church of Russia, Oxford, 1842), public domain. Typed from the page images of archive.org's scan of the printing, read line by line, and compared word for word with the scan's text. The editions' footnotes and their marks are left out, and italics are set plain; the paragraphs are as printed. The section titles name the place in each book. Mouravieff calls him Innocentius Koulchinsky. The 1842 page prints "dictricts"; it is kept as printed.

sections.title: A History of the Church of Russia, pp. 280-281
sections.citation: A. N. Mouravieff, A History of the Church of Russia, ch. XVI, pp. 280-281, tr. R. W. Blackmore (A. N. Mouravieff, A History of the Church of Russia, Oxford, 1842)
paragraphs: By degrees the true faith shed its light also on the Southern dictricts, and the parts about the distant Irkutsk, where there were by this time a good number of Christians, manifested their desire to have a bishop. Innocentius Koulchinsky, who had been appointed head of the spiritual mission to Pekin, was consecrated the first bishop of Irkutsk, and laid there a good foundation for the Church, being celebrated for the holiness of his character during life, and for the discovery of his relics uncorrupted after death.
